subject: Clarify: Pen Test Coverage for Shared Services, Dedicated Pools, and VPC Endpoints
messages:
From: John Park <john.park@acme-analytics.com>

Cc: laura_bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>

Subject: Pen test artifacts + scope questions for Acme proof-of-concept

Hi Soojin,

Thanks again for the demo last week. Our security team is preparing the SIG and a targeted SOC2 checklist for the PoC and asked for the latest penetration test artifacts and a short write-up enumerating which hosting variants are covered by Redwood's internal PT

Specifically they want clarity on two things:
- Is the June 2027 PT report inclusive of (a) Hosted API (multi-tenant control plane + shared inference), (b) Dedicated pools (reserved GPU clusters for a single tenant), (c) Private/VPC deployments where Redwood manages control-plane components in the customer's VPC, and (d) customer on-prem deployments?
- Does the testing include shared-control-plane services (billing, model catalog, routing) that interact with tenant request metadata, or is that explicitly out of scope?

Could you also point us to an asset list or network ranges we can provide to our network team?

Appreciate a short written summary we can attach to the SIG. If helpful, we can schedule a 30-minute call later today.

Thanks,
John Park
Security Engineer
Acme Analytics

Subject: Re: Pen test artifacts + scope questions for Acme proof-of-concept

Hi John — thanks for the note. High-level answers below and I attached the June PT report plus an asset inventory extract. Short summary first, then specifics per hosting mode.

Summary (TL;DR):
- Hosted API: IN-SCOPE for the 2027 PT. The tests covered the multi-tenant runtime (request routing, inference runtime, KV/prefix cache interactions) and the control plane services visible to customers (model catalog APIs, auth/session endpoints). Customer data stores (tenant-managed S3 buckets) were not spun up for the test and are considered out of scope unless explicitly included in a separate contract.
- Dedicated pools: IN-SCOPE when Redwood is operating the reserved GPU clusters. Our PT included the dedicated node set and associated orchestration components (scheduler, cache routing).
- Private/VPC deployments: PARTIAL — in cases where Redwood operates control-plane components (managed control plane in a customer VPC), those control-plane services are in-scope; customer-managed compute (instances owned/operated by the customer in their VPC) were out-of-scope.
- On-prem: OUT-OF-SCOPE by default — the on-prem appliance package is treated as a separate delivery and is only in-scope if we arrange a specific engagement with the customer for testing.

Details / boundaries:
1) Shared/control-plane services: The June 2027 PT explicitly tested the public control-plane endpoints (auth, model catalog, routing). The assessor had authenticated test accounts and exercised session handling, token lifecycle, parameter validation, and a subset of the routing rules. Internal platform admin tooling and billing backends were NOT fully fuzz-tested and are considered limited-scope items. We can add those to scope on request.

2) Dedicated pools: When a customer purchases a Dedicated pool, Redwood deploys tenant-isolated worker pools and a routing policy that pins requests to that pool. The PT included lateral movement checks between pinned pools and the rest of the cluster and validated isolation at the control-plane routing layer and GPU process boundaries.

3) Private/VPC variants: There are two flavors we see: (A) Managed control-plane in customer VPC (we run control-plane components in customer's cloud account) — those components were tested when the customer environment was part of the engagement. (B) Customer-managed stacks (customer installs the inference runtime themselves) — out-of-scope unless we run the engagement.

4) On-prem appliances: We have not included on-prem appliance testing in the June report. That requires an air-gapped assessment and separate logistics.

Attachments included in this reply: redwood_pt_report_20270601.pdf (full findings and remediation table), asset-inventory_20270614.csv (trimmed list of services and DNS entries). Also attaching a text file with the network ranges used for outbound egress from our hosted clusters (network-ranges-20270614.txt).

Open items / remediation status: the attached PT report has a remediation summary. Briefly: 6 medium findings (token handling hardening, ephemeral key rotation cadence, one SSRF vector validated and mitigated), 2 low. Most items were covered by configuration changes and are marked as "remediated" in the report; we listed a small set of follow-on fixes targeted for Q3. If your SIG requires evidence, we can provide PRs/commit ids for the configuration fixes and a short remediation attestation.

Next steps:
- I can send a one-page scope statement you can attach to your SIG (I will draft that if you confirm).
- If you want network ranges and a CIDR list for firewall allowlisting, the attached network-ranges file should suffice; let us know if you need an IP range in a different format.
- Happy to jump on a call — I’m available at 4pm PT today.

Regards,
Soojin Lee
Head of Security & Compliance
Redwood Inference

Thanks, Soojin — very helpful. A couple follow-ups from our network and crypto teams:
1) For managed control-plane-in-VPC mode, do you provide a list of the subnets and specific egress IP ranges used by your control plane? Our infra team needs explicit CIDRs (not just service names).
2) How does customer CMK (KMS) usage affect PT scope — if we bring our own keys and Redwood only sees ciphertext, does that change what the assessor tested or what evidence we should attach to SIG?
3) Do you have a concise scope statement we can drop into the SIG (one-paragraph + bullet list of included/excluded systems)?

If you can reply with the CIDR file and a one-paragraph scope statement, that should be enough for now.

John

John — quick answers inline and attachments included.

1) CIDRs/subnets: see attached network-ranges-20270614.txt — I also added a small CSV with the expected source/destination pairs our infra team uses. If you need the ranges in a different region (e.g., us-east-1 vs us-west-2) call that out and we’ll split them by region.

2) Customer-managed CMK (KMS): If you use a CMK that never exposes plaintext to Redwood (we only see ciphertext and we do not hold key material), the PT did not test customer key material. Evidence for the SIG in that case should be the KMS policy attestation and the configuration showing Redwood services have Encrypt/Decrypt only via customer-granted roles — we can produce the policy snippet and an attestation PDF. If you plan to use Redwood-managed keys, then the PT did include key management for those services and you can reference the PT findings.

3) One-paragraph scope statement (feel free to paste into SIG):

"Redwood Inference penetration testing (June 2027) covered Redwood-operated multi-tenant hosted inference runtime, public control-plane endpoints (authentication, model catalog, routing), and Redwood-operated Dedicated GPU pools. Where Redwood operates control-plane components within a customer's VPC (managed control-plane-in-VPC), those components were included in scope. Customer-managed compute resources (customer-owned VMs, on-prem appliances, or customer-controlled VPC compute) are out-of-scope unless a separate engagement is arranged. Billing backends and internal admin tooling were limited-scope and are not fully covered by the standard PT engagement; these can be included on request."

I’ve attached network-ranges-20270614.txt (CIDRs), redwood_pt_report_20270601.pdf (full report), and asset-inventory_20270614.csv.

If you want the remediation attestation and the PRs linked in the report, we can provide those under an NDA addendum — want me to loop Legal?

Thanks,
Soojin
Head of Security & Compliance
Redwood Inference
